title: Ten minutes to spend
hook: One activity can use time another activity could have used.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: A toy animal has 10 minutes total. Which schedule spends more time feeding: 8 feeding and 2 watching, or 4 feeding and 6 watching?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: A toy animal has 10 minutes total. Which schedule spends more time feeding: 8 feeding and 2 watching, or 4 feeding and 6 watching?

claims.text: A toy animal has 10 minutes total. Which schedule spends more time feeding: 8 feeding and 2 watching, or 4 feeding and 6 watching? Both toy schedules total 10 minutes. The first spends 8 minutes feeding and the second spends 4, so the first has 4 more minutes of feeding. This bookkeeping illustrates a time budget; it does not measure real food intake or safety.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A toy schedule has 3 minutes watching out of 10, with all remaining time feeding. How many minutes feed? 10 total minutes minus 3 watching leaves 7 feeding.
